idea: Construction cost inflation index and commentary for investors
buyer: Real estate and infrastructure funds, contractors' investors
pain: Cost inflation destroys development returns and nobody tracks it investably
verdict: Compounding proprietary data at her exact intersection; slow to build but genuinely ownable.

why.distribution: Fund contacts on the buy side and construction contacts for data; both warm.
why.demand: Cost data is bought routinely in construction; the investor-facing version is untested.
why.fmf: Needs both construction cost literacy and investment framing - her intersection precisely.
why.revenue_structure: Annual data subscription, the stickiest structure available.
why.defensibility: A proprietary index compounds every quarter and cannot be back-filled by a competitor.
why.leverage: Pure data product - one index serves every subscriber.
why.time_to_revenue: An index needs several quarters of history before anyone pays: 6-9 months.
why.tailwind: Cost volatility is real but not structurally increasing.
why.ceiling: £1,000/mo x 17 subscribers = £204k, reachable but only after the index has credibility.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,000/mo x 17 subscribers = £204k less ~£15k data collection = £189k. But nobody subscribes to an index with one quarter of history, so year one is largely unpaid construction. Realistic: £25-45k.
carries: The most defensible idea in the entire set - a proprietary time series compounds and cannot be copied.
kills: Time to revenue. An index is worth nothing until it has history, so year one pays almost nothing.
test: Ask three funds whether they would pay for a credible construction cost index, and three contractors whether they would contribute data.
test_pass: Both sides say yes - that is a two-sided validation.
test_fail: Funds say BCIS or Arcadis already covers it.
